clue.text: Dire Straits: music performers?

indicators.note: dire means dreadful or in a bad state, so the following word's letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A nod to the rock band Dire Straits, asking whether they count as music performers.
explanation.walkthrough: The band name looks like a single unit, but 'Dire' is the anagram signal working on STRAITS. The question mark admits the definition is loose: performers are only one kind of artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording performers are commonly called artists in the music business, as in a label's roster.

clue.text: Approach cold church to pinch animal? On the contrary

indicators.note: to pinch suggests one thing gripping another inside it
On the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the animal does the pinching

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cold church approached by someone trying to steal an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, the cold church would pinch the animal; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles so ASS holds C and CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Access means a way in or a means of approaching a place, as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Have a meal in attempt to get agreement

indicators.note: in places the eating inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: Negotiators sit down to dinner hoping to reach an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Clarity from Sicily — it condemned imprisoning politician

indicators.note: imprisoning means the shuffled letters lock the politician inside them
condemned suggests something ruined or wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A Sicilian court condemning and jailing a politician, presented as a clear verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' looks like part of the courtroom story, but it signals the anagram, and 'imprisoning' signals the container; 'from' just links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplicity of style or expression means plainness and ease of understanding, close to clarity.

clue.text: It could emanate from his tea, maybe

definitions.text: It could emanate from his tea, maybe

indicators.note: emanate from means come out of, so the letters come out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Vapour rising from a man's cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the letters sit inside 'his tea, maybe', and vapour does rise from a hot cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Water vapour rises from a freshly poured hot drink, so the clue describes what comes off the cup.

clue.text: Perhaps help the Queen with transport in street

indicators.note: in places the queen and the transport within the abbreviation for street

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen
a van is a vehicle used for transport

explanation.surface: A royal household scene: the help bringing the Queen's car round to the street.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the late Queen's royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina. 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a domestic servant is one kind of help.
explanation.definitionFit: Household staff are often called the help, and a servant is one such domestic employee.

clue.text: One surrounded by smell is beginning to tell someone in laboratory?

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the numeral inside the word for smell

parts.note: a scent is a smell
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the opening letter of tell

explanation.surface: A smelly person in a lab, perhaps, starting to tell on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: a laboratory worker is often a researcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Researchers in the natural sciences typically work in labs, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Think highly of judge

definitions.meaning: to think highly of someone is to ... them, as in to ... a player
to judge is to assess or value something

explanation.surface: Respecting someone and assessing them in the same breath.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both rating something well and evaluating or appraising it.

clue.text: Every year abolish almost everything by end of January

indicators.note: by means next to, so the last letter follows on after the other pieces
almost means the word for abolish stops one letter short

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or abolish
all means everything

indicators.note: end of takes the closing letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A resolution to scrap nearly everything at the end of each January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' attaches to 'abolish', trimming ANNUL to ANNU, while 'everything' gives ALL whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means once a year, recurring yearly, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Doctor stayed with us for 24-hour periods?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor stayed with us for day-long stretches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person, but it is the verb meaning to tamper. The question mark admits the definition is by example: each named weekday is one such day.
explanation.definitionFit: Each weekday lasts a day, so these are examples of day-long periods.

clue.text: Elite middle-distance runner having secured first in Edinburgh

indicators.note: the runner holds the letter fast inside, as if having secured it

parts.note: Steve Cram was a famous British middle-distance runner of the 1980s

indicators.note: first in picks out only the opening letter of the Scottish capital's name

explanation.surface: An elite athlete competing in Edinburgh after securing first place.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram was a British world-record holder over the mile and 1500 metres; his surname wraps around E.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best part, the elite, as cream rises to the top of milk.

clue.text: Being sixteen involved acne on a regular basis

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters of the number are mixed up
taking every other letter of the skin complaint, regularly spaced, gives the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Being sixteen means dealing with acne regularly, a teenager's lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SIXTEEN into EXISTEN; 'on a regular basis' takes the second and fourth letters of ACNE, C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun means the state of living or having reality, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Yorkshire town intended to avoid a deal

parts.note: Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire

indicators.note: to avoid says the word for intended steers clear of the letter a

parts.note: meant is a synonym of intended

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire town meant to dodge some agreement or business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: SETTLE is a small market town in North Yorkshire, England; 'to avoid a' drops the A from MEANT to leave MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is an agreement reached between parties, as in a divorce or legal deal.

clue.text: Group of musicians prohibited on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard over the airwaves, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: banned means prohibited

explanation.surface: A group of musicians whose song is barred from radio play.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is an ensemble of players performing together, such as a rock or brass group.

clue.text: Urged bravery in final

indicators.note: in places the bravery inside the word for final

parts.note: the end is the final part
courage is bravery

explanation.surface: A coach urging bravery from the team in the final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' reads as a cup match in the surface, but here it is a noun meaning the last part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage someone is to spur or urge them on, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Need friend every now and then

parts.note: occasion can mean need or reason, as in having no occasion to complain
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone who needs a friend from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Need' as a noun matches the older sense of occasion: cause or necessity.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at irregular intervals, now and again, a direct synonym of the clue phrase.

clue.text: These characters in books could be ok

definitions.text: These characters in books could be ok

parts.words: These characters in books could be ok
parts.note: every second letter of the word books is O and then K, so the clue describes which letters are picked

explanation.surface: A reader deciding that the characters in some novels are fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means letters, not people in a story: taking every other letter of BOOKS leaves O and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Every second letter, taken in turn, are the ones described; the clue defines by showing them in action.

clue.text: Cost rose dreadfully for children's toys

indicators.note: dreadfully means badly, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Complaining that the price of children's toys has risen terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Kick scooters are wheeled ride-on toys popular with young children.

clue.text: Popular undergarment with gold angel

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a vest is a British undershirt
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An angel dressed in a trendy vest and gold, like a nativity costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angel' is theatre slang for a backer who funds a show, not a heavenly being. In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang a backer who puts money into a production is called by this heavenly name.

clue.text: State of health's contentious — it alters when losing energy

indicators.note: alters says the letters are changed into a new order
when losing marks one letter to be dropped from the pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A contentious medical claim that someone's state of health changes when they run low on energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alters' rearranges CONTENTIOUS plus IT, and 'when losing energy' means one E is lost from that pool first.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's constitution is their physical make-up and general health, as in a strong constitution.

clue.text: Is upset with National Farmers' Union? Student's wicked

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: the NFU is the National Farmers' Union in Britain
L, from the learner plate on a car, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A student upset with the farmers' union, judged to be wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: The NFU is the British farmers' trade body. L is the learner-driver plate. The 's of Student's reads as 'is' and links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinful and wicked both describe immoral behaviour, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Goes in two hospital departments with son

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, and ER is the emergency room

explanation.surface: A patient going in to two hospital departments with their son.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means goes into a place, same tense and person as the clue phrase.

clue.text: Nothing to write? That's clear

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, stands for nothing
to pen something is to write it

explanation.surface: Having nothing to write leaves the page clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear and open both describe something unobstructed or plain, as in an open view or clear road.

clue.text: In favour of drink before start of inspection, on balance

indicators.note: before puts the drink ahead of the next letter in the answer

parts.note: pro means in favour of
port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: start of takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone who favours a drink before an inspection, on balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on balance' looks like a set phrase, but 'on' is a piece and 'balance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Proportion means harmonious relation of parts, the sense of balance in a design or a sense of perspective.

clue.text: Some music in a pub's turned up, creating alarm

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters climb upward, read backwards
some means a part of the words that follow, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Music in a pub cranked up so loud it causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like loud volume, but in a down clue it reverses CINAP, the run of letters taken from 'music in a pub'.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden fear or alarm, a direct synonym.

clue.text: American broadcast flipping song

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word for broadcast is read backwards

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An American broadcaster flipping out over a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses AIR to RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Amuse nurse

definitions.meaning: to amuse is to keep guests or an audience diverted
to nurse an idea or hope is to harbour it or hold it in mind

explanation.surface: A nurse who amuses patients, or an order to amuse a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to harbour a thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the verb: diverting people, and harbouring a notion as one might a grudge.

clue.text: Foreman ignoring last mistake

indicators.note: ignoring last means the final letter of the word for foreman is left off

parts.note: a gaffer is British slang for a foreman or boss

explanation.surface: A foreman overlooking the latest mistake on site.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER is British informal for a boss or foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or embarrassing error, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Chap making a comeback in certain title inherited from parent

indicators.note: in places the turned-round chap inside the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: man is a synonym of chap

explanation.surface: A man making a comeback, certain of inheriting a title from his father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'title' suggests a peerage, but it is the name one is called by, passed down the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A family name is usually passed down from a parent and serves as a person's title of address.

clue.text: Pampers Charlie with strange French article

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
odd means strange
les is the French plural definite article

explanation.surface: Someone named Charlie fussing over an odd French item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pampers' looks like the nappy brand, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle is to overindulge or treat too tenderly, the same as to pamper.
